summary: Point Verde light at the southern entrance to Placentia Roads, Placentia Bay: established 1879, steel tower from 1990, grounds and tower closed, listed as unstaffed.

light.fog_signal: horn, 4 s blast (interval disputed: 60 s Rowlett; 94 s Lighthouse Friends from 1912)
light.note: Coast Guard list (dated 2026-09-24): Fl W 4s, flash 1 s and eclipse 3 s. Rowlett: white flash every 5 s, focal height 30 m. The record's Wikidata entry gives Fl W 5s. Lighthouse Friends: a fixed white light in the first station; from 1920 one-second flashes, fourteen a minute.

structures.note: Coast Guard list: square skeleton tower, red and white square daymark, 11.3 m. Rowlett: 11 m (37 ft) square steel skeletal tower with an enclosed white lantern. Lighthouse Friends: put in place 1990, with the fog signal and a shed inside a chain-link fence. The record's Wikidata figure is 11.0 m.
Height disputed: Lighthouse Friends 3.7 m; Rowlett 6 m (20 ft). Rowlett says it had to be removed because of shoreline erosion. The removal date is not given.

structures.type: square pyramidal, open frame, on enclosed base
structures.note: Carried a new acetylene light made by Chance Brothers of Birmingham, England. Lighthouse Friends: the enclosed wooden tower of the old lighthouse was removed at this time.

structures.type: square pyramidal, wood, octagonal lantern, painted red and white
structures.note: Built at some time during Joe Greene's service (about 1922 to 1945); Lighthouse Friends gives no closer date.

structures.type: rectangular two-storey dwelling with square tower above the roof
structures.note: First station on a cement foundation, with a sixth-order lens and a fixed white light at a 30 m focal height (Lighthouse Friends). The dwelling portion was kept for the keeper when the wooden tower was removed in 1920.
Flat-roofed fog alarm building 9.1 m north of the lighthouse (Lighthouse Friends). Its present state is not given.

staffing.note: The Fisheries and Oceans brochure (page modified 2019-09-24) lists Pointe Verde among the unstaffed lightstations. Lighthouse Friends says the light was staffed until the early 1970s, but its own keeper list runs to 1991; the Encyclopedia says it was automated in the early 1970s.

access.note: Site and tower closed (Rowlett); grounds and tower closed (Lighthouse Friends). The Canadian Coast Guard owns the station.

events.note: Petition to the House of Assembly for a light at Point Verde, presented by a Mr. Dwyer; cost noted at about $4,000 (Lighthouse Friends).
Design prepared and carried out in 1878; lantern room ready by the year's end, but the lighting material had not arrived from Scotland (Lighthouse Friends).
Rowlett: station established 1879. Lighthouse Friends does not give a lighting date. The Encyclopedia's 'two years later' after its 1874 figures would be 1876; see resolved_conflicts.
September 1880 inspection: facing peeling off the concrete foundation walls, rot revealed; worst parts repaired before winter, rest the following year (Lighthouse Friends).
Iron fastenings added to the tower against gale working; tightened in 1887 (Lighthouse Friends).
December gale shook the lighthouse and blew away the privy (Lighthouse Friends).
Flat-roofed fog alarm building 9.1 m north of the lighthouse; four-second blast every 94 seconds (Lighthouse Friends).
New square pyramidal open-frame tower with acetylene light by Chance Brothers; flash of 1 s every 3.28 s dark, fourteen a minute. Enclosed wooden tower removed (Lighthouse Friends).
Joe Greene begins looking after the light, around 1922 (Lighthouse Friends).
On Joe Greene's death, son Leonard made keeper (Lighthouse Friends).
Encyclopedia: automated in the early 1970s. Lighthouse Friends: staffed until the early 1970s. Its keeper list runs to 1991.
Cylindrical fibreglass tower erected: 3.7 m (Lighthouse Friends) or 6 m (Rowlett), removed later because of shoreline erosion (Rowlett).
Square steel skeletal tower with enclosed lantern put in place, with a fog signal and shed inside a chain-link fence (Lighthouse Friends; Rowlett).

corrections.why: The Coast Guard list (dated 2026-09-24) gives 11.3 m for the square skeleton tower. The record's 11.0 m comes from Wikidata.
The Fisheries and Oceans brochure (page modified 2019-09-24) lists Pointe Verde among the unstaffed lightstations.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Coast Guard list (dated 2026-09-24): Fl W 4s. Rowlett (undated): a white flash every 5 s. The record's Wikidata: Fl W 5s. The Coast Guard list is the most recent official entry and is recorded.

Rowlett: station established 1879. Lighthouse Friends: lantern room ready by the end of 1878 but the lighting material late from Scotland. The Encyclopedia (as reproduced) says 'two years later' after its 1874 population figures, which would be 1876. The record keeps 1879; the story says 'the late 1870s'.
Lighthouse Friends: 3.7 m. Rowlett: 6 m. Neither is dated more closely; the story gives both.

DFO brochure (2019): unstaffed. Lighthouse Friends' text: staffed until the early 1970s. Lighthouse Friends' keeper list: keepers to 1991. Encyclopedia: automated in the early 1970s. The story states the disagreement.
Rowlett: blast every 60 s. Lighthouse Friends: four-second blast every 94 seconds from 1912. Dates of change not known.

notes_for_editor: The history rests almost entirely on Lighthouse Friends, which in turn draws on the Journal of the House of Assembly (the 1877 petition, the 1878 works, the 1880 inspection) and the Encyclopedia of Newfoundland and Labrador. None of those volumes was read. The Encyclopedia text is a Library and Archives Canada reproduction of the ENL entry; the original online entry (enl.cuff.com) was not read. Its 'two years later' follows the 1874 population figures and would put the lighthouse in 1876; this is unresolved, and the story keeps 1879 from Rowlett. Lighthouse Friends' keeper list starts James E. Croucher in 1878, a year before Rowlett's establishment date. Its text and its own keeper list disagree after 1970 (see resolved_conflicts). Keepers after 1960 (Leonard Greene, Thomas Green, Leo McGrath, George Thomas) are named only as Lighthouse Friends prints them, in their public role, with no personal detail. Joe Greene's wife Louise is mentioned only for her efforts as Lighthouse Friends reports them; she did not keep the light. Facebook group posts and genealogy forum posts about the Greene family appeared in search results; they are private individuals and were not used. A Whoa Dana blog post was not used. The Canadian Marine annual reports in the corpus name no Point Verde light. A Chronicling America search for 'Point Verde' returned no relevant page. The federal heritage designations CSV does not list the station. Wikipedia (Division No. 1, Subdivision B) appeared in search results as a lead only and was not used. The 2010 staffing list in the record was not re-read (Senate report not read for this station). Fact-check (2026-10-28): the story now states the first-lighting disagreement: the Encyclopedia's 'two years later' after its 1874 figures would give 1876, while Rowlett gives 1879; Lighthouse Friends' keeper list starts James E. Croucher in 1878. Later towers (1912 fog alarm, 1920 tower, the wooden tower of Greene's time, 1975, 1990) are placed in Building the light, following the guide. The lantern-room sentence now says the tower was 'ready to receive its lantern room', as Lighthouse Friends does; the earlier wording said the lantern room was ready.
